chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: A week with Teddy Hill's slave-driving band at the Apollo
summary: Teddy Hill kept trumpet players blowing without rest, the hardest working band Cheatham ever played with, and he left after a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I see, but you also at that time, did you go with Teddy Hill's band?
Yes, I worked with Teddy Hill's band, I think one week at the Apollo Theater. That band was working me so hard, I couldn't make it.
Now who was with the Teddy Hill band at the time?
Now the only person I can remember now, was a bass player, Dick Fullbright. He's the only person I can remember.
Oh, yeah. Dizzy wasn't with him?

Could've been -- he could've been. I don't remember, I worked so hard at that Savoy, played so many shows that I was glad that I couldn't make it any farther with that band, hardest working band I ever played with in my life.
What was so hard about it?

Well, Teddy Hill was a -- he's what we call like a slave driver, he'd keep the band blowing without regards to trumpet player's lips, they tire, you just keep them blowing all the time and screaming, you have to give a

trumpet player a little rest now and then, but there were band leaders like that that didn't realize a trumpet player had to take his horn down from his lips, you can't be screaming all night long, it's impossible and I think his band was too hard, it was one of the hardest blowing bands I've ever known.
